decisionsTitle: Each person waiting sees where they stand in the line, and the event page says how many wait (amending §348, §587, §612, §615)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-01**, in his own words, as relayed with the request: «Acum mai am nevoie de încă o setare cu "lista de așteptare e publică"». The line was read as the thread of the waiting list's visibility the club has been working through (§396's public list of states, §587's count on the event page, §615's «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare»): what a person waiting is told about the line, and what the page tells everybody. This section builds the two parts of it that need no new setting and no disclosure — **each person sees where they stand, and the event page says how many wait** — and leaves the word «setare» to the owner (see the open question below): nothing here makes the list of names more public.

### What happened until now

A person on the waiting list was told they were «Pe lista de așteptare» and nothing else: not how long the line was, nor how far they were from the front. The registration's own page showed no state at all for a single registration (only a family's card has the state chip), «Toate înscrierile mele» showed the chip, and the `WAITLIST_JOINED` email said «te-am adăugat pe lista de așteptare. Te vom anunța dacă se eliberează un loc.» The event page said how many wait in some states and not in others: «3 pe lista de așteptare» as a line of its own when places were free, «… — 3 așteaptă deja un loc» in the full state's lead, and nothing at all on the places line (§615: «150 înscriși din 150 de locuri — 133 confirmați, 17 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare»), nor when the line was full or the event kept none.

### The decision

**A. Where a person stands.** One sentence, «Ești pe locul 3 din 10 persoane de pe lista de așteptare.», then one on how freed places go. It appears in three places, from one reader:
1. **The registration's own page** (`/registrations/manage/<token>`): under the state — a one-person page gets the state's words as a heading, «Pe lista de așteptare», which it never had, and the sentence under it; a family's card has the state chip, so only the sentence.
2. **«Toate înscrierile mele»**: the same sentence on a `WAITLISTED` row, under the date.
3. **The `WAITLIST_JOINED` email**: «Când am trimis acest email erai pe locul 3 din 10.» / "When we sent this email you were number 3 of 10." — one sentence added after the body, in both halves, worded as of the moment of rendering because an email is read later and the line moves. Never «ești» in an email. It is a machine-added sentence after the body whoever wrote it, like the other facts of a send (§547, §588): a club that rewrote the message's words still sends it.

**One reader, the allocator's order.** `readWaitlistPosition(db, registrationId)` in `registrations/repository.ts` returns `{ position, length, autoOffer }`, or null when the registration is not `WAITLISTED`. The position is `row_number() over (order by waitlisted_at asc, id asc)` among the event's `WAITLISTED` rows — `lockOldestWaitlisted`'s own order, the one the allocator offers places in, written as a window over the same rows rather than as a second statement of the rule — and the length is the count of those rows. An offered person (`WAITLIST_OFFERED`) has left the line; a cancelled or expired row never was; `kind` appears in no condition, so a `TEST` row stands in the line like a real one (`AGENTS.md` §12.6), as `countEligibleWaitlisted` counts it. Two statements, no lock: a number one place stale the instant it renders is the same as the public counts, and nothing is decided from it. `listManagedPeople` and `listActiveRegistrationsForParticipant` carry it (`waitlistStanding`) on a waiting row only, one read each; a row that is not waiting costs nothing.

**Honest about the order (§615).** The second sentence follows the event's «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» as it stands when the page is read: on «Da» «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.»; on «Nu» «Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.» — the page never promises an order the club has not kept. `autoOffer` comes from the same read of the event row, so no page makes a second query for it. The email carries no order sentence: it is read later, and the setting can change between the send and the reading — a promise in an email is the one that outlives the setting.

**The words.** `Registrations.waitlist` in both catalogues: `position.{one,few,other}` through `countForm` on the line's length («din 1 persoană», «din 10 persoane», «din 20 de persoane»; English repeats its one form under the three keys), `orderAuto`, `orderClub`. The email's words are in `templates.ts` as every email's are: two numbers and no noun to agree with them, so no plural form. No number is typed in code.

**The email reads the position at render time, and why.** The renderer already has the database and the registration the outbox row names (`registrationId`), as it has for every other fact of a send (`render.ts`); the template itself has none. A number written into the payload at queue time would be as old as the queueing — and an email is rendered at send time, again at every retry, and again on a staff resend, each after the line moved — so the payload carries nothing new and the sentence is «as of the moment I was rendered». When the person is no longer waiting at render time (an offer was made, they cancelled) the sentence is simply absent.

**Privacy.** The sentence is on the registration's own token page and in its own email, and says two numbers about the line and nothing about anybody else: no name, no state of another person. The public list is not touched (`StartList.tsx`, §396, §613): it still shows no position.

**B. The event page says how many wait.** The places line (`fillPhrase`) gains a last part, «10 pe lista de așteptare» ("10 on the waiting list"), whenever anybody waits: «150 de înscriși din 150 de locuri — 133 de confirmați, 17 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare, 10 pe lista de așteptare». The number is `readPublicPlaces`'s `waitlisted` — the `WAITLISTED` rows with no offer yet, from the same count the door already reads and the public cache carries, with no second query; a test registration stands in it as in every public count (and cannot exist in production). It rides on `PublicFill` (`waitlisted`, set by `publicFill`, absent when nobody waits and in a cache entry from before the halves were counted). It reuses the existing `cta.waitingCount` words.

**Not twice in one card.** Each state of the page says the number once:
- **Open, with a places line** (a capped event): the places line carries it, and the separate «N pe lista de așteptare» line it used to have beneath the free-place count (§587, §612) is gone — the same words, moved into the line where the other counts are. An uncapped event has no places line and no waiting list, so nothing changes there.
- **Full, the line takes people:** the lead already says «… — 3 așteaptă deja un loc.» (§587, the owner's words of 2026-09-30), the places line leaves it out (`fillPhrase(…, { withWaiting: false })`), so the card does not say the same number in two registers. The lead's count is the whole line (waiting plus an open offer), as it was.
- **The line full, or no list at all** (a sentence and no button): there is no lead with a number, so the places line says it.
- **The listing card** (`CardRegistration`) has no places line and was already consistent: the open state's detail carries the offered and the waiting counts (`openLinePhrases`), the full state's lead the count. Unchanged.

### Rejected
- **A position on the public list.** The list shows the confirmed, and — behind the notice (§396) — the ticked pending and waiting, each with its state and no position; a position beside a name is a disclosure the privacy notice does not describe. Not touched.
- **A position written into the email's payload at queue time.** Stale at the first retry; see above.
- **A promise of order in the email.** The setting can change before the email is read.
- **A second count query for the event page.** `waitlisted` is already in the cached read.
- **A new setting for any of this.** None needed: the sentence follows the setting that exists.

### Open question for the owner
«O setare cu "lista de așteptare e publică"» may mean a per-event switch for showing the waiting list's names on the public list (today only the privacy notice's `{{participantListStates}}` decides it, §396, for every event at once). That is a disclosure rule and is not built here; his word decides whether it is a per-event setting, and what it would show.

### Consequences
`registrations/repository.ts` (`readWaitlistPosition`); `registrations/domain/waitlist-standing.ts` (the type); `registrations/ui/waitlist-position-words.ts`; `registrations/manage-family.ts` and `registrations/my-registrations.ts` (`waitlistStanding`); the two token pages; `notifications/render.ts` and `templates.ts` (`waitlistStanding`, `waitlistPosition`); `events/domain/registration-cta.ts` (`PublicFill.waitlisted`), `events/ui/counted-phrases.ts` (`fillPhrase`), `RegistrationCta.tsx`, `registration-door.ts`; `messages/{ro,en}.json` (`Registrations.waitlist`). The allocator, the capacity formula, `waitlist.ts` and the public list are untouched. No migration, no dependency. Tests: `unit/registrations/waitlist-standing-words.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/waitlist-position.test.ts`, `integration/notifications/waitlist-joined-position.test.ts` (new), `unit/events/counted-phrases.test.ts`, `unit/events/registration-cta.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/registration-fill-render.test.ts`.
changelogLine: - **«Ești pe locul 3 din 10 persoane de pe lista de așteptare»** — each person waiting sees their place in the line and how freed places go (in order, or the club chooses) on their own page, in «Toate înscrierile mele» and, as of the moment it was sent, in the waiting-list email; the event page's places line ends with how many wait. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a registration on the waiting list, when its own page (the manage link) or «Toate înscrierile mele» is opened, then under its state it says «Ești pe locul {n} din {m} persoane de pe lista de așteptare.» / "You are number {n} of {m} on the waiting list." — {n} is 1 plus the `WAITLISTED` registrations of the event ahead in the allocator's own order (`waitlisted_at`, then `id`) and {m} every `WAITLISTED` registration of the event, from one reader (`readWaitlistPosition`); Romanian's three forms through `countForm` on {m}; a one-person page shows the state's words as a heading above it; a registration that is not waiting shows no such sentence; an offered, cancelled or expired registration is not in the line, a `TEST` registration is, and the sentence names nobody else (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

While the event's «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» is on, the sentence adds «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» / "Freed places are offered in order."; while it is off it says «Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.» / "The club chooses who is offered a freed place." and promises no order; the setting is read as it stands when the page is opened (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The places line of the event page — in every state that shows it — ends with «{n} pe lista de așteptare» / "{n} on the waiting list" whenever anybody is `WAITLISTED` (`readPublicPlaces`'s `waitlisted`, the cached count the door already reads, no further query, a test registration counted as in every public count), after the confirmed, in-progress and kept parts: «150 de înscriși din 150 de locuri — 133 de confirmați, 17 în curs de confirmare, 4 locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare, 10 pe lista de așteptare»; with nobody waiting the line is as it was; the number is said once in a card — in the full state the lead's «… — {n} așteaptă deja un loc.» carries it and the places line leaves it out, and the open state's separate «{n} pe lista de așteptare» line is the places line's part (amends criterion 11) (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The position a waiting person is told is the order the allocator offers places in: given three waiting registrations, the one with the earliest `waitlisted_at` reads «locul 1», a tie on the instant is broken by stable id, and when the person ahead is offered a place the next one reads «locul 1» at the next opening of the page (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a `WAITLIST_JOINED` message, when it renders, then after its body — whoever wrote it — it adds one sentence in each half's own language, «Când am trimis acest email erai pe locul {n} din {m}.» / "When we sent this email you were number {n} of {m}.", worded as of the moment of rendering, never as a present state; the numbers are read at render time from the same reader as the registration's own page with the registration the outbox row names (not from the payload, so a retry or a resend says the line as it is then); nothing is added once the registration is no longer waiting, nor to any other message, and no other person is named (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: each person on the waiting list sees where they stand; the places line says how many wait
